sources.title: Sale of Government of India Treasury Bills/Cash Management Bill by Auction
sources.issuer: Government of India, Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs
sources.retrieval_method: Chrome Save As from the official RBI-hosted PDF URL; no access-control challenge was bypassed

verification.clause_2_i: Bills may have maturities up to 364 days; auction particulars are announced by RBI.
verification.clause_2_iv: Bills are issued at a discount and redeemed at face value.
verification.clause_5_v: Successful bidders deposit the requisite amount by the prescribed cut-off on the auction settlement day.
verification.clause_7: Bills are issued as Promissory Note / credit to SGL account with RBI.
verification.clause_9: Bills are repaid at par on expiration of tenor at the RBI office where registered.

sources.provenance_limit: The retained official RBI-hosted URL ends GOI27032018_TBill.pdf. RBI's 2024 auction notice links a similarly dated attachment ending GOI27032018_A.pdf. The identity/equivalence of those two files was not established; do not claim byte equivalence.
unresolved_from_document: No explicit holiday or business-day adjustment for a T-bill maturity.
No exact intraday time when redemption proceeds become available.
No evidence that same-day maturity proceeds can fund an auction bid.

sources.title: The Government Securities Act, 2006 and The Government Securities Regulations, 2007 — FAQ
sources.review_status: official page reviewed online; raw page bytes not retained
sources.relevant_question: Q36 says holders of securities in SC, BLA, SGL/CSGL may use automatic redemption, with maturity proceeds credited to the investor's bank account on the due date if bank details are provided to RBI or its agent.
sources.scope_limit: General Government-security FAQ. It does not state a T-bill-specific holiday rule, an intraday credit time, or actual account-level performance.
